intro: Boolean retrieval answers an exact membership question. Required terms narrow the candidate set, and excluded terms remove documents even when other terms match.
task: Resolve required and excluded query terms against posting lists, including unknown terms and repeated document IDs.
requirements: postings is a dictionary from nonempty strings to lists or tuples of integer-valued document IDs in [0,1000000]; duplicates and unsorted lists are allowed.

required and excluded are token lists or tuples of at most 10000 nonempty strings. required must be nonempty. Return a sorted Python list of IDs present for every required term and for no excluded term.
An unknown required term makes the result empty. Unknown excluded terms have no effect. Repeated query terms do not duplicate results.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Use set operations
hints.body: Intersect required-term document sets, then subtract excluded-term sets.

hints.title: Sort once at the boundary
hints.body: Return stable ascending IDs after all membership operations are complete.

explanation: Boolean retrieval is independent of ranking: a document either satisfies every condition or it does not. Set intersection expresses all required terms, while set difference handles exclusions.
Missing required terms must produce no results. Treating them as absent query constraints would silently broaden the query and return incorrect documents.
